route_summary.notes: The A2A team implements the requested payment button, then QA identifies two integration concerns: status-gating of the button and the retained run.py legacy-default path. The process expands from the page feature into launcher behavior, README launch-path documentation, server-level HTTP tests and launch-path tests. Frontend removes status gating, backend changes CHECKOUT_COMPAT default from on to off, QA/reviewer re-verify the broader state, and release lead finalizes with explicit non-blocking pre-GA follow-ups.

semantic_nodes.semantic_state: Request a payment button on the checkout page that works with the existing checkout flow.
Frontend creates the pay-button UI and checkout POST flow, producing the requested page-level feature.

Integration review broadens the process model from the page feature to two system conditions: GET /api/status should not gate payment, and run.py still defaults into the retired compatibility handler that returns 410 on POST.
Backend changes current-launch behavior by switching run.py's default compatibility setting from on to off and adds launch-path/server-level regression coverage plus launch-path documentation.
Frontend removes status gating so the button is enabled by default and disabled only while the checkout request is in flight.
QA repeatedly re-verifies the landed page, API, launcher and test state and reports the hardcoded cart as a non-blocking residual gap.
Reviewer confirms release readiness, adds non-blocking pre-GA concerns (real cart wiring, invalid-cart UX, idempotency and telemetry), but does not trigger further repository mutation.
Release lead finalizes the feature and broader integration work; the terminal checkpoint preserves both the requested UI change and launcher/test/documentation changes.

cpr_events.summary: A pre-update compatibility authority remains embedded in the current run.py launcher and is reopened during an otherwise current feature task; this historical residue becomes operationally relevant to the current execution path and drives a downstream scope change.

The realized action surface expands from adding a checkout-page button into changing launcher default behavior, updating launch-path documentation, and adding new launch-path/server-level regression suites. These are material code/test/documentation changes outside the page module itself, even though they improve integration robustness.
The launcher and frontend conclusions are grounded in direct frozen code state, tests and re-verification; no unsupported semantic descendant replaces independent evidence.
